text:
Kyle: Heads-up — I pushed a draft Grafana row that correlates per-model batch amplification with KV cache hit-rate. Putting it under /dashboards/tmp/batch-amplifier. Wanted feedback on queries and sensible alert thresholds.

autoscale-bot: dashboard updated: /dashboards/tmp/batch-amplifier at 2026-03-18T10:03:10Z :white_check_mark:

Maya: Nice, can you paste the PromQL you used? I want to compare to the existing queue-depth panel.

Kyle: Sure, two queries I used for the panels (simplified):

```
# average batch size over 5m per model
avg by(model) (rate(inference_batch_size_sum[5m]) / rate(inference_batch_size_count[5m]))

# kv cache hit rate per model
sum by(model) (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum by(model) (rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))
```

Kyle: And a derived "batch amplification" metric I charted as avg_batch_size / avg_single_token_batch (we have a gauge for single-token baseline per model):

```
avg by(model) (rate(inference_batch_size_sum[5m]) / rate(inference_batch_size_count[5m]))
/
avg by(model) (model_single_token_baseline)
```

Hyun: Hmm — curious about noise on small-traffic models. We should only show models with >= 50 requests / 5m or else amplification spikes look wild. Add a filter like `sum by(model) (rate(inference_requests_total[5m])) > 50`.

Maya: Agree. Also for alerts: suggestion: trigger when queue depth > 120 *and* amplification < 1.4 *and* kv cache hit rate < 0.6 for the last 5m. That usually indicates saturation + cold cache. Thoughts?

Hyun: Sounds reasonable. I'd also require autoscaler hasn't scaled in last 3m to avoid alerting during planned scale-ups. We have metric `autoscaler_scaling_events_total`. Example alert expression:

```
alert: BatchAmplificationSaturation
expr: |
  (
    sum by(model) (rate(inference_queue_depth[5m])) > 120
    and
    (
      avg by(model) (rate(inference_batch_size_sum[5m]) / rate(inference_batch_size_count[5m]))
      /
      avg by(model) (model_single_token_baseline)
    ) < 1.4
    and
    (sum by(model) (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum by(model) (rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))) < 0.6
  )
  and
  (increase(autoscaler_scaling_events_total[3m]) == 0)
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Model {{ $labels.model }} showing queue saturation and low amplification"
  runbook: "https://confluence.redwood.com/runbooks/inference-saturation"
```

Kyle: I like that. For dashboards: propose three small panels per model row — queue_depth, batch_amplification, kv_cache_hit_rate — with a small sparkline for 1h and a large alarm indicator if alert firing. Keep it compact so we can add many models.

Maya: Good. Also add an annotation layer that shows recent deploys and config changes (autoscaler policy tweaks). It helps triage whether low amplification is due to a recent rollout.

Hyun: Can we also expose the prefix/KV cache size gauge (`kv_cache_total_keys{model}`) so product teams see if caches are undersized? Sometimes hit-rate recovers after cache size bump.

Kyle: Will add that. Next steps: I'll update the dashboard to filter out low-traffic models, add the scaling-suppression clause to the alert, and create a small runbook blurb for on-call.

Maya: Assign a follow-up: @Hyun can you review the alert for noisy false positives after we rollout? Hyun: will do, add me to the alert test group.

autoscale-bot: created alert rule `BatchAmplificationSaturation` in staging (rule id: 4372).

Kyle: Thanks — I'll PR the dashboard JSON to infra/dashboards and include links to the queries + the runbook. :thumbsup:

Maya: If we get repeated pages for the same model, we should consider an automated temporary throttling or fallback to a lower-capacity model variant. That could be a later automation step.

Hyun: Agreed. For now, let's focus on getting the panels and alert stable.

Kyle: filing follow-up checklist in #eng-infra: add dashboard PR, alert PR to production, runbook entry, and add Hyun to alert test group.

Maya: Thanks — ping here when it's live and I'll add a tile to the SLO dashboard.
